userText:
Building: Hôtel de Ville, Paris (city hall).
The front (−z) is the west front on the Place de l’Hôtel-de-Ville.
Footprint: 144.1 m along x by 89.1 m along z, centred on the origin.
Outline (approximate: the hull of its OpenStreetMap parts), [x, z] in metres, going round:
[[-72.1,-40.9],[-71,-41.7],[-29.9,-44.5],[27.4,-44.6],[71,-41.4],[72,-39.5],[72.1,40.6],[71.3,41.5],[38.4,44.5],[29.1,44.6],[-38.2,44.5],[-71.2,40.6],[-72.1,39.8]]
Height: the highest point is 55 m above the ground.

3 photographs attached, in order:
  1. front three-quarter across the square: central clock tower, corner pavilions and steep slate roofs, daylight
  2. three-quarter from a bridge along the river side, showing the long wing, towers and mansard roofs
  3. view along the long flank facade with its repeated arched bays and mansard roof

Reply with the JSON object only.

json.notes: The three biggest differences: first, the model is open at the back, so the court has no rear wing, but the real building is closed all round the outline, with its inner court reached through the building. Second, the central clock tower is too slight, with a narrow shaft and small spire, so it does not dominate the front as it does in the photographs. Third, the corner pavilions are not separate enough from the wings, so the front reads as one roof mass. I close the court and widen the tower, keeping its 55 m height.

json.notes: The Hôtel de Ville is a pale stone palace built round a large court, with a rusticated ground floor, two pilastered storeys and a steep grey mansard roof with dormers. Its two corner pavilions rise above the body under tall French pavilion roofs. The central clock tower with its belfry and slender spire rises over the middle of the west front, and I am modelling all four as the signature masses.
